weeks.title: Settling in: s, a, t, p

spell.rule: s a t p (tricky word: I)

weeks.read: A rhyming picture book – pause before the rhyming word and let your child fill it in

days.ma: Sock pairs: tip out a pile of clean socks and match the pairs together, counting each pair aloud as you make a pile (stop at 5).
days.en: Sound walk: stand still in the garden or a room, close eyes for one minute and listen, then take turns saying what you heard. Introduce s as a hissing snake and hunt for three things that start with s.

days.ma: Teddy tea party: give each toy one cup and one spoon, saying 'one for you, one for you'. Is there one each, or are some left over?
days.en: Introduce a (ants crawling up your arm) and t (tap the table). Play I-spy with sounds: 'I spy something beginning with t'.

days.ma: Stair count: climb the stairs together counting 1 to 5, then jump back down saying 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, blast off!
days.en: Introduce p (puff out a candle). Say s-a-t, p-a-t and t-a-p slowly like a robot; your child shouts the word and does an action.

days.ma: Make piles of 1, 2 and 3 toy cars or spoons and ask 'which pile has the most? Which has the fewest?'
days.en: Write s, a, t, p big in chalk outside or with a finger in a tray of flour; trace each one together while saying its sound.

days.ma: Quick check: show 1 to 5 fingers quickly; your child copies with their own fingers and tells you how many.
days.en: Quick check: point to s, a, t, p on scraps of paper in any order for a sound each, then blend at, sat and pat together. Spot the word I in a book.

weeks.title: Numbers 1 to 3; sounds i, n, m, d

spell.rule: i n m d (tricky words: the, to)

weeks.read: A picture book with a simple repeating pattern your child can join in with

days.ma: Find 1, 2, 3: hunt the house for one spoon, two shoes and three pegs and line them up in order.
days.en: Introduce i (wiggle fingers like an itchy insect) and n (make a 'nnn' aeroplane noise). Sort a pile of toys: which start with n?

days.ma: Peek-a-boo dots: draw 1, 2 or 3 dots on scraps of paper, flash one for a second and ask how many – no counting allowed, just looking.
days.en: Introduce m (rub your tummy, 'mmm') and d (bang a pretend drum). Robot talk: say m-a-p and d-i-p and your child says the word.

days.ma: Tower of three: build towers of 1, 2 and 3 bricks and put them in order from shortest to tallest, saying the number of each.
days.en: Read the repeating book together and stop before a page turn: 'What do you think will happen next?' Then turn and check.

days.ma: Jump to it: call out 1, 2 or 3 and your child does that many jumps, claps or stamps, counting aloud.
days.en: Write i, n, m, d with a wet paintbrush on a fence or path, saying the sound as you form each letter; watch them dry and do it again.

days.ma: Quick check: show 1, 2 or 3 dots or fingers for a second; can your child say how many at a glance?
days.en: Word fishing: write sat, pin, man, dad and tip on paper fish; your child 'catches' one, reads it by blending, and keeps it. Find 'the' on a page.

weeks.title: Numbers 4 and 5; sounds g, o, c, k

spell.rule: g o c k (tricky words: no, go)

weeks.read: A library picture book about animals – talk about what each animal is doing

days.ma: Five fingers: show 5 fingers in different ways (4 and 1, 3 and 2) and ask 'Is it still five?' Then try 4 the same way.
days.en: Introduce g (gurgle like water down a drain) and o (say 'o' as you flick a light on and off). Find things in the kitchen starting with g or o.

days.ma: Egg box count: put dried pasta or buttons into an egg box, one per hole, touching and counting each one up to 4 or 5.
days.en: Introduce c and k – two letters, same sound. Click your fingers 'c, c, c'. Blend c-a-t, k-i-t and d-o-g aloud.

days.ma: Who has more? Give two teddies different handfuls of up to 5 bricks; your child counts each and says who has more.
days.en: Picture chat: look at a page of the animal book and ask 'What can you see? What is the dog doing?' Encourage a full-sentence answer.

days.ma: Hopscotch to 5: chalk squares numbered 1 to 5 on the ground and hop along saying the numbers, then hop back.
days.en: Go and no: write 'go' and 'no' on two cards and play traffic lights – your child reads the card you hold up and moves or freezes.

days.ma: Quick check: tip out 4 or 5 objects; can your child say how many, then make a group with the same amount?
days.en: Quick check: read got, cat, dog and kid from cards, then say a sound (g, o, c, k) for your child to point to.

weeks.title: Seeing amounts; sounds ck, e, u, r

spell.rule: ck e u r (tricky words: I, into)

weeks.read: A non-fiction library book about ducks, farm animals or pets

days.ma: Dice snap: roll a die and say the number of dots without counting, then fetch that many toys.
days.en: Introduce ck (two letters, one sound, as at the end of duck) and e (tap your elbow). Hunt for a sock, a rock or a clock and say the ck at the end.

days.ma: Finger flash: hide your hands, then show some fingers for two seconds – how many did your child see?
days.en: Introduce u (put up an umbrella) and r (roll like a dog 'rrr'). Robot talk with r-e-d, s-u-n and d-u-ck.

days.ma: Dot plates: draw dice patterns for 1 to 5 on paper plates or paper, spread them out and your child runs to the one you call.
days.en: Mealtime chat: take turns telling one thing you did today and ask a 'why' question about it. Wait for the answer and reply to it.

days.ma: Ladybird spots: draw ladybirds with 1 to 5 spots; your child puts the matching number of buttons next to each.
days.en: Spell it: say 'sun', tap the three sounds on three fingers together, then your child writes s-u-n with chalk or a crayon.

days.ma: Quick check: flash the dot plates; score a point for each amount named without counting.
days.en: Quick check: read bed, duck, rug and kick and do an action for each. Spot I and into in a book.

weeks.title: More, fewer, same; sounds h, b, f, ff

spell.rule: h b f ff (tricky words: no, go, the)

weeks.read: A traditional tale with a wolf who huffs and puffs – told from memory or from a library book

days.ma: Snack compare: make two plates of up to 5 raisins or pieces of fruit. Which has more? Which has fewer? Now make them the same.
days.en: Introduce h (pant like a dog) and b (bounce a ball). Collect three things beginning with h or b and say the first sound of each.

days.ma: Toy rows: line up two rows of toys side by side, one opposite one; which row has more, and how can you tell?
days.en: Introduce f and ff (ff sits at the end, as in off and puff). Read huff, puff and off, blowing a tissue each time.

days.ma: Shoe count: make a pile of grown-up shoes and a pile of children's shoes; count and say which pile has more.
days.en: Read or tell the wolf tale. Talk about the new words in it (huff, puff, straw, chimney) and what they mean.

days.ma: Fair or unfair: give two teddies different numbers of bricks; your child says who has more and makes it fair.
days.en: Retell the tale using toys as characters, using story words such as 'once upon a time', 'next' and 'in the end'.

days.ma: Quick check: show two groups (such as 3 and 5 spoons); your child points to the group with more, then fewer, and explains how they know.
days.en: Quick check: chalk h, b, f and ff on the ground and call a sound to hop on, then read hat, big and off.

weeks.title: Making 4 and 5; sounds l, ll, ss

spell.rule: l ll ss (tricky words: to, the, into)

weeks.read: A bedtime story with lots of characters – count the characters together

days.ma: Five in the bed: lay 5 toys on a towel; roll some out and count how many are in bed and how many are out.
days.en: Introduce l (lick a lolly) and ll (as at the end of bell and doll). Tap a spoon on a glass each time you say a word with l in it.

days.ma: Hidden hands: hide 4 buttons in your two hands; open one hand – how many must be in the other?
days.en: Introduce ss (a hissing snake at the end of hiss and mess). Blend hiss, kiss, mess and fill.

days.ma: Two colours: make 5 using two colours of pegs or pasta in different ways (4 and 1, 3 and 2) and say each one.
days.en: Read captions together: 'a big red bus', 'a doll in bed'. Your child points to each word as you read.

days.ma: Stair split: put 5 toys on two stairs, some on each; how many different ways can you share them out?
days.en: Tall letters: write l, b, d, h and k with a chunky pencil on the back of an envelope, starting each at the top.

days.ma: Quick check: show 5 fingers, fold some down and ask 'How many are hiding?'
days.en: Quick check: your child reads 'a doll in a bed' and 'the bell is on the hill' and draws a picture to match.

weeks.title: Consolidation: Phase 2 sounds and numbers to 5

spell.rule: Review all Phase 2 sounds from s to ss (tricky words: I, no, go, to, the, into)

weeks.read: Re-read your child's favourite book from this half term

days.ma: Number hunt: spot the numbers 1 to 5 on things around the home (clock, oven, remote control) and do that many star jumps for each.
days.en: Sound bingo: write 9 Phase 2 letters in a grid; call sounds and your child covers each with a coin or button.

days.ma: Dice and dots: roll a die, say the amount at a glance and collect that many pegs; keep going until someone has 10.
days.en: Robot word race: say any word from the list in robot sounds (d-o-g); your child blends it and points to something that matches.

days.ma: Which has more? Hide up to 5 small toys in each hand; your child picks a hand, counts both and says which had more.
days.en: Story recall: re-read a favourite book; your child tells you the bits they remember and what they liked best.

days.ma: Car park: make 5 with toy cars in two 'car parks' drawn on paper; how many different ways can you park them?
days.en: Label it: write a label for a toy such as 'a red bus' or 'a big dog'. Your child sounds it out and writes it – any sensible spelling counts.

days.ma: Celebration check: count to 5 and back, name some dice patterns at a glance and show 5 two ways on fingers.
days.en: Quick check: hide I, no, go, to, the and into on paper around a room; your child reads each one as they find it.

weeks.title: Numbers 6, 7, 8; sounds j, v, w

spell.rule: j v w (tricky words: he, she)

weeks.read: A picture book with a surprise ending – guess the ending before you read it

days.ma: Count on: do 6 claps, then 2 more stamps – how many altogether? Try 7 and 1, then count everything as high as you can go.
days.en: Introduce j (wobble like jelly) and v (vroom like a van). Blend jam, jet, van and vet.

days.ma: Five and a bit: make 6 with one full hand and 1 finger, 7 with a hand and 2, 8 with a hand and 3. Spot the pattern.
days.en: Introduce w (blow like the wind). Draw a spider's web and write web, wet, win and wig on it to read.

days.ma: Autumn collection: gather 8 leaves, sticks or stones outside, line them up and count, touching each one.
days.en: Read the surprise-ending book, stopping before the end: 'What do you think will happen?' Then read on and check.

days.ma: Step numbers: stick numbers 1 to 8 on the stairs; your child stands on the step you call and counts on to the top.
days.en: Weekend talk: help your child say 'I went to … and then I …' about the past, and 'Tomorrow I will …' about the future.

days.ma: Quick check: ask for 6, 7 or 8 objects from a bigger pile; can your child stop at the right number?
days.en: Quick check: read he and she on cards, then read 'he is wet' and 'she has a jet'.

weeks.title: Numbers 9 and 10; sounds x, y, z, zz, qu

spell.rule: x y z zz qu (tricky words: we, me, be)

weeks.read: A library book of nursery rhymes – learn one new rhyme off by heart

days.ma: Ten frame: draw two rows of five boxes (or use an egg box with ten holes) and fill it with 9, then 10, pieces of pasta.
days.en: Introduce x (as at the end of box and six) and y (yawn 'y'). Read box, fox, six and yes.

days.ma: Keep counting: count star jumps past 10 to see how far you get together; listen for the 'teen' numbers.
days.en: Introduce z and zz (buzz like a bee) and qu (two letters, quack like a duck). Blend zip, buzz, quiz and quack.

days.ma: Skittles: stand up 10 empty plastic bottles or toilet rolls, roll a ball, and count how many fell and how many are standing.
days.en: Rhyme time: say a nursery rhyme together, then invite your child to ask you a question about it ('Why did he fall?').

days.ma: Ten toes: count toes, then fingers, touching each one, then count both together past 10.
days.en: Spell it: say fox, zip and yes; your child taps the sounds on fingers then writes each word with chalk or a crayon.

days.ma: Quick check: flash the ten frame with 6 to 10 filled; how many pieces? How many empty spaces?
days.en: Quick check: write we, me, be, he and she on paper; call one and your child splats it with a hand.

weeks.title: Comparing to 10; sounds ch, sh

spell.rule: ch sh (tricky words: was, my)

weeks.read: A non-fiction library book about the sea or boats

days.ma: Fruit bowl: count the apples and the other fruit (or two kinds of pasta, up to 10); which has more, fewer or the same?
days.en: Introduce ch (choo-choo train). Find ch in chin, chop and much, chugging your arms each time you hear it.

days.ma: Grab and compare: take turns grabbing a handful of pegs, count them, and say who has more and who has fewer.
days.en: Introduce sh (finger on lips, 'sh'). Read ship, shop, fish and dish, and sort them into sh at the start and sh at the end.

days.ma: Set the table: count the people and the plates; are there enough forks? How many more do you need?
days.en: Pretend shop: set up a toy shop; take turns as shopkeeper and customer, asking and answering 'How much?' and 'Have you got…?'

days.ma: Bigger wins: write 1 to 10 on scraps of paper; each player picks one and the bigger number wins the round.
days.en: Word explorer: read the sea book and pick two new words (such as 'shell' or 'crab'); use each in a sentence together today.

days.ma: Quick check: show two groups up to 10; your child says which has more and explains how they know.
days.en: Quick check: read 'a fish in a dish' and 'my ship was red'; your child draws one of them.

weeks.title: Shape and pattern; sounds th, ng

spell.rule: th ng (tricky words: you, they)

weeks.read: A traditional tale with a king or queen

days.ma: Shape hunt: find circles, squares, triangles and rectangles around the home; count the sides and corners of each.
days.en: Introduce th (poke your tongue out a little: this, that, thin). Read this, that, then and moth.

days.ma: Spoon patterns: make a repeating line of fork, spoon, fork, spoon… What comes next? Then try red, red, blue.
days.en: Introduce ng (as in ring, king and sing). Sing a favourite song and listen for words that end in ng.

days.ma: Clap patterns: clap, stamp, clap, stamp; your child continues, then makes up a pattern for you to copy.
days.en: Read the king or queen tale, then your child draws three pictures – beginning, middle, end – and retells it in their own words.

days.ma: Shape pictures: tear or cut paper into shapes and make a house or rocket; which shape is the biggest? Which is the smallest?
days.en: Letter shapes: write th, sh, ch and ng with a finger on a steamed-up window or in a tray of flour, saying the sound each time.

days.ma: Quick check: put a few household objects in a pillowcase; feel one and describe its shape for the other person to guess.
days.en: Quick check: read 'the king can sing a long song', then find you and they in a book.

weeks.title: Number bonds to 5; sounds ai, ee

spell.rule: ai ee (tricky words: her, all)

weeks.read: A picture book about the weather

days.ma: Part-part-whole: draw a big circle joined to two small circles; put 5 buttons in the big one, then split them into the two small ones in different ways.
days.en: Introduce ai (rain on the roof). Read rain, tail, wait and sail, wiggling fingers like rain for each ai.

days.ma: Two hands: 'I have 5 pieces of pasta; there are 2 in this hand – how many in the other?' Swap roles.
days.en: Introduce ee (what can you see?). Read see, bee, feet and seed, making a buzzing bee fly to each word.

days.ma: Hop together: hop 3 times then 2 more; how many altogether? Try 4 and 1, then 5 and 0.
days.en: Read the weather book; ask your child what they noticed and let them ask you a question about it.

days.ma: Bath ducks: put 5 toys in the bath or a bowl, 2 swim away; how many are left? Say it as a sentence together.
days.en: Read captions: 'see the bee', 'a tail in the rain', 'wait for her'. Your child reads each and acts it out.

days.ma: Quick check: show 5 fingers, fold some down, and your child says the bond (3 and 2 make 5) without counting.
days.en: Quick check: sound race – write ai, ee, sh, ch, th and ng; how fast can your child say every sound?

weeks.title: One more, one less; sounds igh, oa

spell.rule: igh oa (tricky words: are, was, my)

weeks.read: A night-time or bedtime story

days.ma: Stair steps: stand on step 4; go up one – which step now? Down one – which step now?
days.en: Introduce igh (three letters, one sound, as in night). Read high, light, night and right, reaching up high on each one.

days.ma: Tower plus one: build a tower of 6 bricks; add one – how many? Take one off – how many?
days.en: Introduce oa (a goat in a boat). Read boat, coat, goat, road and soap.

days.ma: Number line hop: chalk 0 to 10 on the ground; stand on a number, then jump to one more and one less.
days.en: Write a sentence: 'a goat in a boat'. Your child says it, counts the words on fingers, then writes it with your help.

days.ma: Paper chain: make a chain of 10 paper strips; tear one off at a time, saying 'one less' and the new number.
days.en: Packing list: write a list for a teddy's trip – 'a coat', 'a hat', 'a sock' – your child sounds out each word.

days.ma: Quick check: say a number up to 9; your child tells you one more and one less.
days.en: Quick check: say 'a boat at night'; your child writes it and reads it back to you.

weeks.title: Consolidation: winter games with sounds and numbers

spell.rule: Review j to oa (tricky words: he, she, we, me, be, was, my, you, they, her, all, are)

weeks.read: A winter story – re-read it twice this week

days.ma: Parcels: wrap small boxes or toys in newspaper and count them; hide some behind your back and ask how many are hiding.
days.en: Sound sort: write ch, sh, th, ng, ai, ee, igh and oa on cards and sort toys and household objects by the sound in their name.

days.ma: Snowball throw: throw rolled-up socks into a basket; count the ones in and out, then compare scores.
days.en: Card writing: write a short message in a homemade card, such as 'to you from me', with your child sounding out each word.

days.ma: Domino dots: match dot patterns on dominoes or homemade dot cards, naming each amount at a glance.
days.en: Retell the winter story with toys as characters, using words from the book.

days.ma: Bond hands: show 5 fingers with some up and some down; your child says how many up and how many down.
days.en: Party plan: plan a pretend winter party together – what will we need and why? Encourage 'because' in each answer.

days.ma: Quick check: one more and one less up to 10, and which of two groups has more.
days.en: Quick check: read tricky words from a pile; any that stick go back in the pile for next week.

weeks.title: Making 6 and 7; sounds oo and oo

spell.rule: long oo and short oo (tricky words: was, you, they)

weeks.read: A non-fiction library book about space or the moon

days.ma: Six on two plates: share 6 grapes or pasta pieces between two plates in different ways (5 and 1, 4 and 2, 3 and 3).
days.en: Introduce long oo (moon, zoo) and short oo (book, look). Say both, then sort words into a 'moon' pile and a 'book' pile.

days.ma: Seven days: count the days of the week on fingers; split 7 into 5 school days and 2 weekend days.
days.en: Read moon, food, look and good; your child points up at the moon for long oo and opens a book for short oo.

days.ma: Car colours: line up 7 toy cars or blocks of two colours; say 'four red and three blue make seven'. Change them round.
days.en: Read the space book; your child asks you two questions about it and you answer, then swap.

days.ma: Dice pairs: roll two dice and check whether they make 6 or 7 together; collect the pairs that do.
days.en: Word of the day: pick a new word from the space book (such as 'rocket' or 'orbit') and both use it three times today.

days.ma: Quick check: hide part of a group of 6 or 7 under a cup; how many are hiding?
days.en: Quick check: read 'look at the moon' and 'a good book'.

weeks.title: Making 8, 9, 10; sounds ar, or

spell.rule: ar or (tricky words: me, be, all)

weeks.read: A picture book set on a farm

days.ma: Ten frame gaps: fill a ten frame with 8 objects; how many empty spaces? '8 and 2 make 10.'
days.en: Introduce ar (open wide for the doctor). Read car, farm, park and star.

days.ma: Finger nines: show 9 fingers in different ways using both hands (5 and 4, 6 and 3) and say each one.
days.en: Introduce or (toot a horn). Read fork, corn, short and torch.

days.ma: Number stories: '9 birds on a fence, some fly away…' Act it out with toys and say how many stayed and how many flew.
days.en: Why questions: look at a farm picture and ask 'Why do you think the farmer needs a tractor? Why is the barn big?'

days.ma: Two rows of five: lay 10 toys in two rows of five and see that 10 is 5 and 5; move one across – now what?
days.en: Spell it: say park and fork; your child taps the sounds and writes them, remembering ar and or are two letters.

days.ma: Quick check: show 8, 9 or 10 on a ten frame for a moment; how many? How many more make 10?
days.en: Quick check: read 'a star in the dark' and 'a short fork'.

weeks.title: Number bonds to 10; sounds ur, ow

spell.rule: ur ow (tricky words: her, my, they)

weeks.read: A story with an owl or other night-time animals

days.ma: Skittles to 10: knock over some of 10 bottles; the standing ones and the fallen ones make 10. Say the pair.
days.en: Introduce ur (a nurse with a purse). Read fur, turn, hurt and burn.

days.ma: Finger partners: show some fingers; your child puts up the rest of their fingers to make 10 together.
days.en: Introduce ow (ow! a cow stepped on my toe). Read cow, now, down, town and owl.

days.ma: Bond hop: chalk 0 to 10; your child stands on a number and counts the hops to reach 10.
days.en: Read the owl story, then your child retells it using 'first', 'next', 'then' and 'in the end'.

days.ma: Ten in the bed: 10 toys on a blanket; some roll out; how many in, how many out?
days.en: Read a sentence: 'turn the car down the road' – your child reads it, pointing to each word.

days.ma: Quick check: call a number 0 to 10; your child shouts its partner to make 10.
days.en: Quick check: read her, my and they, then 'they can see a cow'.

weeks.title: Doubles; sounds oi, ear

spell.rule: oi ear (tricky words: are, you, all)

weeks.read: A funny picture book – talk about what made you laugh

days.ma: Mirror doubles: put 1 to 5 buttons in front of a mirror; how many can you see now? 'Double 2 is 4.'
days.en: Introduce oi (boing like a spring). Read coin, oil, soil and join.

days.ma: Double dice: roll one die, then make the same amount again with toys – say 'double 3 is 6'.
days.en: Introduce ear (hear with your ear). Read ear, hear, near, dear and beard.

days.ma: Butterfly spots: draw a butterfly, put spots on one wing and the same on the other; count all the spots.
days.en: Talk time: chat about something your child did yesterday and will do tomorrow, modelling full sentences joined with 'and' or 'because'.

days.ma: Doubles at home: socks, shoes, hands, eyes – count one, then both; how many altogether?
days.en: Sentence starter: write 'I can hear a …'; your child finishes it with their own idea and writes it.

days.ma: Quick check: a quick doubles quiz up to double 5, using fingers if needed.
days.en: Quick check: read 'a coin in the soil' and 'can you hear me?'

weeks.title: Odd and even, sharing; sounds air, ure, er

spell.rule: air ure er (tricky words: he, she, we, was)

weeks.read: A story with three tries or three characters – guess what the third will do

days.ma: Sock partners: pair up 6 socks, then 7 socks; with odd numbers one is left without a partner.
days.en: Introduce air (fair hair). Read air, hair, pair and chair.

days.ma: Fair shares: share 8 pieces of pasta between two teddies, then share 7; what happens to the last one?
days.en: Introduce ure (are you sure?) and er (a better letter). Read sure, cure, letter and hammer.

days.ma: Two by two: march toys into a box in pairs; which amounts make perfect pairs and which leave one out?
days.en: Read the story and stop at three points to guess what happens next, especially before the third try.

days.ma: Odd or even path: write 1 to 10 in chalk; hop only on numbers that can be shared into pairs (2, 4, 6, 8, 10).
days.en: Listen and do: give three instructions in a row ('touch your nose, hop twice, sit down') for your child to follow, then swap.

days.ma: Quick check: give your child up to 10 objects; they pair them up and say odd or even.
days.en: Quick check: read 'a pair of chairs' and 'a better letter'.

weeks.title: Consolidation: all the new sounds and numbers to 10

spell.rule: Review all Phase 3 sounds (tricky words: he, she, we, me, be, was, my, you, her, they, all, are)

weeks.read: A favourite book from the library chosen by your child

days.ma: Make 10 hunt: collect 10 small things; split them between two bowls and say the pair each time you change them.
days.en: Digraph dash: write 10 of the new sounds (such as sh, ai, igh, oo, ar) around a room; call a sound and your child runs to it.

days.ma: Doubles snap: roll a die and say the double; check by making it with toys.
days.en: Read along: your child reads one page or one line from the library book to a toy.

days.ma: Compare and fix: make two piles of up to 10; say which has more and how many to move to make them equal.
days.en: New words: pick three interesting words from this half term's books and act each one out for the other to guess.

days.ma: Odd or even sort: count piles of 1 to 10 pegs and put them in an 'odd' box or an 'even' box.
days.en: Write a sentence about something you did this week, such as 'I had a good week'; your child writes it.

days.ma: Celebration check: bonds to 10 with fingers, one double and an odd or even question.
days.en: Quick check: read chair, moon, park, coin and light, then three tricky words.

weeks.title: Counting to 20; reading with ch, sh, th, ng

spell.rule: Review ch sh th ng in longer words (tricky words: you, they, are)

weeks.read: A counting book that goes up to 20

days.ma: Count to 20: count stairs, then keep going on the way back, or count jumps to 20 in the garden.
days.en: Sound hunt: find sh, ch, th and ng in the counting book or around the house (shoe, chair, the, ring).

days.ma: Teen numbers: make 13 as a ten frame of 10 plus 3 more; try 15 and 18.
days.en: Read shell, check, much and thing; your child acts each one out after reading it.

days.ma: Twenty pegs: peg 20 clothes pegs around a bucket or box, counting each one; then take them off counting backwards from 10.
days.en: Back-and-forth chat: play 'Would you rather…?' and both explain your answers.

days.ma: Number line: write 1 to 20 on paper strips and peg them in order on a string or lay them on the floor.
days.en: Show and tell: your child chooses a toy and tells you three things about it, using a new word.

days.ma: Quick check: count to 20 forwards, then from 10 back to 0.
days.en: Quick check: read 'a moth on a long thing' and 'they are on a ship'.

weeks.title: Counting past 20; reading with ai, ee, igh, oa, oo

spell.rule: Review ai ee igh oa oo (tricky words: all, her, was)

weeks.read: A story about a journey

days.ma: Big count: count toys, pasta or stairs past 20; notice that 21, 22, 23 follow the same pattern as 1, 2, 3.
days.en: Sound sort: write ai, ee, igh, oa and oo on paper and sort the word list under the right sound.

days.ma: Clap count: count claps to 30, clapping louder on 10, 20 and 30.
days.en: Read the journey story; your child retells where the character went in order, using a toy to show the journey.

days.ma: Bundles of ten: group pasta, sticks or pegs into tens; count the tens and the ones left over.
days.en: Read a sentence: 'a sheep in the rain' – your child reads it and draws a picture.

days.ma: Twenty-something: count out loud from 18 to 28 bouncing a ball, then from 25 to 35.
days.en: Letter writing: practise the letters in rain, feet, boat and night, starting each one in the right place.

days.ma: Quick check: start at a number such as 19 or 26 and your child carries on counting.
days.en: Quick check: read rain, feet, light, boat and moon, then all, her and was.

weeks.title: 3D shapes and position; reading with ar, or, ur, ow, oi

spell.rule: Review ar or ur ow oi (tricky words: said, so)

weeks.read: A picture book that shows where things are (under, behind, on top)

days.ma: Shape sort: find boxes, tins, balls and tubes in the kitchen; which roll, which stack, which do both?
days.en: Sound sort: write ar, or, ur, ow and oi and sort the word list under them.

days.ma: Hide and seek teddy: hide a toy and give clues using 'under', 'behind' and 'next to'; then swap.
days.en: Spell it: say down, farm and coin; your child writes them, choosing the right letters for each sound.

days.ma: Tallest tower: build towers with boxes and tins; which is tallest? Which shapes are best at the bottom?
days.en: Read the 'where' book and talk about new position words, using them to describe things around you.

days.ma: Dot flash: arrange up to 5 buttons in different layouts and flash them – can your child still see how many at a glance?
days.en: Why does it roll? Ask your child to explain why a ball rolls and a box does not.

days.ma: Quick check: name a 3D shape (ball, box, tube) and your child finds one at home and says if it rolls.
days.en: Quick check: read 'turn down the park' and say 'said' and 'so' from cards.

weeks.title: Measuring; two-syllable words

spell.rule: Review ear air ure er, plus two-syllable words (tricky words: have, like)

weeks.read: A non-fiction book about growing things

days.ma: Longer or shorter: compare spoons, socks and shoes; line them up from shortest to longest.
days.en: Two-part words: clap the two beats in rocket, carpet and garden, then read each part and push them together.

days.ma: Heavy and light: hold two objects, one in each hand; which is heavier? Check with a coat-hanger balance if you like.
days.en: Read sunset, pocket and farmer by covering one half, reading it, then reading the other half.

days.ma: Full, half full, empty: pour water between cups in the bath or sink and describe each one.
days.en: Read the growing book; your child asks you questions about it and comments on what surprised them.

days.ma: Taller than me: find things in the house that are taller or shorter than your child, and things about the same.
days.en: Spell it: your child writes 'I like…' and finishes it with a word of their choice.

days.ma: Quick check: give three objects to put in order of length or weight, and say which is longest or heaviest.
days.en: Quick check: read 'I have a rocket' and 'a fair garden'.

weeks.title: Number stories to 10; reading and writing captions

spell.rule: Captions and sentences with Phase 3 sounds (tricky words: so, do, some)

weeks.read: A story with a problem to solve

days.ma: Bus story: 10 seats on a toy bus (a box); 6 people get on, how many empty seats? Make up more stories.
days.en: Caption match: write three short captions and draw three pictures; your child reads and matches them.

days.ma: Take away: 7 toys at a picnic, 3 go home; how many are left? Act it out with real toys.
days.en: Read the problem story; ask 'What was the problem? How did they fix it?'

days.ma: Number sentences: say '4 and 6 make 10' with fingers, then '10 take away 4 leaves 6'.
days.en: Write a caption for a photo or a drawing, such as 'the moon at night'.

days.ma: Make 10 snack: share 10 pieces of fruit between two plates in a new way each time and say the bond.
days.en: Listen and draw: read a short sentence aloud ('a fish in a big box'); your child draws exactly what they heard.

days.ma: Quick check: tell a quick number story within 10 and your child answers with a sentence.
days.en: Quick check: your child reads a caption you have written and writes one of their own.

weeks.title: Consolidation: spring review

spell.rule: Review Phase 3 sounds and two-syllable words (tricky words: said, so, have, like, do, some)

weeks.read: Re-read the book your child enjoyed most this half term

days.ma: Counting relay: take turns counting one number each from 1 as high as you can go past 20.
days.en: Sound bingo: grid of Phase 3 sounds; call each and your child covers it.

days.ma: Bond pairs: write 0 to 10 on paper and match the pairs that make 10.
days.en: Read two pages of the favourite book, with your child reading the words they can.

days.ma: Measure challenge: find something longer than a spoon, heavier than a shoe and taller than a chair.
days.en: Feelings chat: talk about the best part of this half term and why, using full sentences.

days.ma: Number line race: jump along a chalk line from 10 to 20, saying each number.
days.en: Write two sentences about a picture your child has drawn.

days.ma: Celebration check: bonds to 10, counting past 20 and a comparing question.
days.en: Quick check: read the word list and say each tricky word.

weeks.title: Take away within 5; blends at the end of words

spell.rule: Adjacent consonants at the end: nd nt mp st lk lp (tricky words: come, were)

weeks.read: A story set outdoors or on a camping trip

days.ma: Five birds: 5 toys on a wall; 2 fly away – how many are left? Answer quickly, then check.
days.en: Blends at the end: say tent, jump and milk slowly – can your child hear both sounds at the end? Read them together.

days.ma: Subtraction hide: put 5 coins under a cup, take some out; how many still under?
days.en: Robot words: say h-a-n-d and l-a-m-p; your child blends them and does an action.

days.ma: Five frogs on a log: sing and act it out with toys, saying '5 take away 1 is 4' each time.
days.en: Camping chat: build a den with a blanket and talk about what you would pack and why.

days.ma: Bond quickfire: you say a number 0 to 5; your child says what goes with it to make 5.
days.en: Spell it: say best, help and lost; your child taps four sounds and writes the word.

days.ma: Quick check: three quick take-away stories within 5 and how many are left.
days.en: Quick check: read 'come to the tent' and 'we were lost'.

weeks.title: Doubling and halving; blends at the start of words

spell.rule: Adjacent consonants at the start: st sp sn sl tr dr fr gr pl cl (tricky words: there, little)

weeks.read: A non-fiction library book about frogs or minibeasts

days.ma: Half each: share 6 or 8 pieces of fruit equally between two plates; 'half of 8 is 4'.
days.en: Blends at the start: read stop, spin and snap, saying both starting sounds clearly.

days.ma: Double it: show a number on one hand and the same on the other; 'double 4 is 8'.
days.en: Read drum, frog, grab and clap, then play a quick game of each action.

days.ma: Folding halves: fold paper in half and cut out a shape; are the two halves the same?
days.en: Why do frogs jump? Read the frog book and ask your child to explain one thing they learnt.

days.ma: Fair share: share 10 toys between two teddies, then 9; can it be done fairly?
days.en: Read a sentence: 'a little frog is there on a plum'.

days.ma: Quick check: doubles to 5 and halves of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
days.en: Quick check: read stop, frog, clap, there and little.

weeks.title: Odd and even again; blends with digraphs

spell.rule: Blends with Phase 3 sounds (tricky words: one, when)

weeks.read: A story with a train or a long journey

days.ma: Odd one out: make piles of 1 to 10 socks; pair them and say which piles have an odd one left over.
days.en: Read train, sweet and float – blend the first two sounds, then the digraph, then the end.

days.ma: Even steps: climb the stairs saying the even numbers loudly and the odd numbers in a whisper.
days.en: Read spoon, green and start; your child acts each word.

days.ma: Which is more? Compare two piles of up to 10 and say how many more one has than the other.
days.en: Read the train story, stopping to guess what happens at the next station.

days.ma: Pattern of pairs: lay pairs of pasta in a line for 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10; what do you notice?
days.en: Spell it: your child writes train, storm and chimp, using a digraph for one sound.

days.ma: Quick check: say a number to 10; your child says odd or even and shows it with paired objects.
days.en: Quick check: read 'when one train can start' and two words from the list.

weeks.title: Counting beyond 20; longer words with blends

spell.rule: Longer words with adjacent consonants: stamp crust plant twist (tricky words: out, what)

weeks.read: A non-fiction book about plants or trees

days.ma: Counting walk: count steps on a walk past 20, 30 or as far as you can; pause on each ten and cheer.
days.en: Read stamp, crust and plant, stamping on each sound.

days.ma: Count with a pattern: count to 30 in a quiet voice and say the tens (10, 20, 30) loudly; spot the repeating 1 to 9 pattern.
days.en: Read twist, frost and blend, then make up a silly sentence using one.

days.ma: Number spot: find numbers above 20 on household items (food packets, clocks, letters) and read them together.
days.en: Read the plant book; your child listens and answers 'What does a plant need?'

days.ma: Big collection: count a big collection of pasta into tens; how many tens and ones?
days.en: Letter practice: write stamp, plant and frost with careful letter shapes.

days.ma: Quick check: count from 17 to 27, then from 25 to 35.
days.en: Quick check: read 'what is out in the frost?' and three words from the list.

weeks.title: Patterns and shape; two-syllable words

spell.rule: Two-syllable words with blends (tricky words: do, so, said)

weeks.read: A book of poems or rhymes

days.ma: Necklace pattern: thread pasta or beads in a repeating pattern; what comes next? Make a tricky one with three colours.
days.en: Clap and read: clap the beats in sandpit and windmill, then read each part and push them together.

days.ma: Shape patterns: make a pattern of shapes with buttons or cut paper; continue and correct a mistake.
days.en: Read lunchbox, helmet and pumpkin, covering half of each word.

days.ma: Dot patterns: make patterns of dots for numbers up to 10 (like dice) – which can be made into two equal rows?
days.en: Poem time: read a short poem twice and talk about the new words in it; your child picks a favourite word.

days.ma: Compare towers: build two towers of up to 10 bricks; which is taller and by how many bricks?
days.en: Picnic plan: write a sentence about a picnic: 'We had a picnic in the sandpit'.

days.ma: Quick check: continue a pattern you start, then explain the rule.
days.en: Quick check: read 'do the children like a picnic?' and 'so said the windmill'.

weeks.title: Consolidation: summer number and reading review

spell.rule: Review Phase 4 blends (tricky words: said, have, like, so, do, some, come, were, there, little, one, when, out, what)

weeks.read: A book your child has heard before – they tell you the story first

days.ma: Number mix: subitise a dot card, make it with fingers, then say its partner to 10.
days.en: Blend it: say words from the list in robot sounds for your child to blend.

days.ma: Doubles and halves: double 2, 3, 4 and 5, then halve 6, 8 and 10.
days.en: Story retell: your child tells the story first, then you read it and compare.

days.ma: Counting game: count past 20 together with each person saying the next two numbers.
days.en: Writing: your child writes a sentence about their favourite part of the book.

days.ma: Comparing: two groups up to 10; which is more, how many more, odd or even?
days.en: Ask me: your child asks you three questions about a picture and you answer.

days.ma: Celebration check: one dot card at a glance, one bond to 10, one double, one odd-or-even and a count from 18 to 25.
days.en: Quick check: read the word list and the tricky words; mark any to keep practising.

weeks.title: Understanding 10; blends with long vowel sounds

spell.rule: Blends with long vowel sounds: tr-ai-n, st-ar-t, fl-oa-t (tricky words: little, one)

weeks.read: A story about growing up or growing things

days.ma: Ten frame tricks: make 10 on a ten frame in as many ways as you can with two colours.
days.en: Read train, start and float, then make up a sentence with one of them.

days.ma: Bonds race: you say a number; your child shows its partner to 10 on fingers as fast as they can.
days.en: Read the growing-up story; stop to predict what the character will do next.

days.ma: Ten in two hands: hide 10 pasta pieces in two hands; open one – how many in the other?
days.en: Talking time: talk about what your child can do now that they couldn't do as a baby, giving reasons.

days.ma: Many ways to 10: show 10 with fingers, toys, jumps and claps.
days.en: Read 'a little spoon on one bright toast' and draw it.

days.ma: Quick check: number bonds to 10 quickfire.
days.en: Quick check: read sweet, brown, sport and bright.

weeks.title: Comparing in real life; compound words

spell.rule: Compound words: sun+light, star+fish (tricky words: said, have, like)

weeks.read: A non-fiction book about the seaside or rock pools

days.ma: Toy shop: price toys 1p to 10p with paper labels and use pretend coins; which costs more?
days.en: Compound words: read sun and light, then sunlight; try starfish and treetop.

days.ma: Puddle compare: after rain, find the longest and shortest puddle or the deepest and shallowest.
days.en: Read handbag, bedroom and toothbrush, splitting them into two words.

days.ma: Height line-up: line up family members or toys from shortest to tallest.
days.en: Read the seaside book; ask your child why a starfish lives in a rock pool.

days.ma: Compare collections: compare two piles of up to 10 and use 'more', 'fewer' and 'the same'.
days.en: Spell it: your child writes sunlight and fishpond, one part at a time.

days.ma: Quick check: compare two groups up to 10 and say which has more and by how many.
days.en: Quick check: read 'I like the starfish' and 'I have a toothbrush'.

weeks.title: Numbers in stories and games; writing sentences

spell.rule: Writing sentences with blends (tricky words: said, have, like, come, some)

weeks.read: A story with a journey or adventure – your child makes up a new ending

days.ma: Story maths: read a story and count characters, objects or pages; who has more?
days.en: Write a sentence: 'I can swing on the swing'; your child writes it with spaces between words.

days.ma: Counting game: play a board game made on paper with a die, counting squares to 30.
days.en: Read splash, string and spring; your child writes one in a sentence.

days.ma: Number line hop: chalk 0 to 20; hop to a number one more or one less.
days.en: New ending: your child says a new ending for the adventure story and you write it down together.

days.ma: Comparing scores: play skittles and compare scores each round.
days.en: Feelings chat: talk about a time your child felt proud, using 'because'.

days.ma: Quick check: count past 20 and compare two numbers up to 10.
days.en: Quick check: your child writes 'I like…' with three of their own ideas.

weeks.title: Bonds to 10 and doubles; all the tricky words

spell.rule: Phase 4 review (tricky words: were, there, little, one, when, out, what)

weeks.read: A favourite book – read it twice this week

days.ma: Doubles snap: roll a die, say the double, then check by showing the same number on both hands.
days.en: Sound race: write every sound learnt this year on a sheet and time how fast your child can say them all; try to beat it on Friday.

days.ma: Bonds to 10 relay: you say 3, your child says 7; swap and speed up.
days.en: Read the favourite book; your child hunts for tricky words on each page and reads them.

days.ma: Sharing equally: share 6, then 7, then 8 pieces of pasta between two plates; which amounts share equally?
days.en: Story retell: your child retells the favourite book using socks or toys as puppets.

days.ma: Odd and even: count out groups of 1 to 10 buttons, pair them up and sort each into an odd or even pile.
days.en: Ask me: your child asks you three questions about your day, and you ask three back, listening to each answer.

days.ma: Quick check: double 1 to 5 and five bonds to 10, as fast as possible.
days.en: Quick check: read this week's tricky words from cards, then the word list.

weeks.title: Review: favourite number games; Phase 2 and 3 sounds

spell.rule: Review Phase 2 and 3 sounds (tricky words: the, to, I, no, go, into, he, she, we, me, be)

weeks.read: A library book chosen by your child

days.ma: Teacher swap: your child chooses a favourite number game from this year and teaches it to you.
days.en: Sound chart: write all the Phase 2 and 3 sounds on a sheet; your child says each one and finds an object for five of them.

days.ma: Dice flash: roll two dice and name each amount at a glance, then say which is bigger.
days.en: Read the library book together; your child reads any words they can sound out and you read the rest.

days.ma: Snack compare: two bowls with up to 10 pieces of fruit each; your child says which has more and makes them the same.
days.en: Retell: your child retells the library book to a toy, using at least one new word from it.

days.ma: Two-box 10: put 10 toys into two boxes in a different way each time and say the pair ('7 and 3 make 10').
days.en: Back-and-forth chat: take turns asking each other about favourite foods, animals or places and why, keeping it going for five turns each.

days.ma: Quick check: count to 20 and back from 10, name three dice rolls at a glance and say which of two piles has more.
days.en: Quick check: read the word list, then splat the tricky words with a hand as you call them out.

weeks.title: Review: patterns, doubles and sharing; Phase 4 blends

spell.rule: Review Phase 4 blends (tricky words: was, my, you, her, they, all, are, said, have, like)

weeks.read: A story with a twist – guess the twist before the end

days.ma: Pattern parade: start a pattern with toys, then actions (jump, clap, clap); your child continues it and makes one for you.
days.en: Blend it: write the word list on scraps of paper and turn them over one at a time for your child to read.

days.ma: Doubles hunt: find doubles around the home (two eyes, four wheels on a toy car shown as 2 and 2) and say each double fact.
days.en: Read the twist story and stop to guess what happens before the end.

days.ma: Fair shares: share 10 pegs between two teddies, then 5 pegs; which shares fairly and which leaves one over?
days.en: Why did it happen? Ask your child to explain why the twist in the story happened, using 'because'.

days.ma: Finger bonds: show some fingers; your child says how many more make 5, then how many more make 10.
days.en: Spell it: say tent, frog and plant; your child taps the sounds and writes each one.

days.ma: Quick check: three doubles, two halves and three bonds to 10, answered as quickly as possible.
days.en: Quick check: read the tricky words from cards, then read 'a frog in the sunlight' and 'they said it was a splash'.

weeks.title: Ready for Year 1: counting and story celebration

spell.rule: Celebration review (tricky words: so, do, some, come, were, there, little, one, when, out, what)

weeks.read: Your child chooses a book to read to you

days.ma: Big count: count as far past 20 as you can together, noticing the pattern.
days.en: Story reading: your child reads a book they can decode to you or a toy, using a finger to track the words.

days.ma: Ten frame show: fill a drawn ten frame with two colours of pasta in as many ways as you can and say each pair.
days.en: Write a sentence about the best thing this year, such as 'I liked the picnic in the garden'.

days.ma: Race to 20: roll a die, say the amount at a glance and hop that many squares along a chalk track to 20.
days.en: Talk about Year 1: what will be the same, what will be new, and how your child feels.

days.ma: Number story: your child makes up a number story within 10 with toys ('8 cars, 3 drive off…') for you to solve.
days.en: Draw and write: draw a picture of yourself in Year 1 and write a caption.

days.ma: Celebration check: count past 20, bonds to 10 and dice at a glance.
days.en: Celebration check: read the word list and tricky words, then choose a favourite book to read together.
